reports.companies_covered: AMZN, JD, ZAL, MELI, CPNG, ETEA.BO, SHOP, PDD
reports.headline: GS sees global eComm compounding at +6% through 2031, prefers scaled platforms, and names MELI its LatAm stock pick.
reports.summary: GS frames global eComm as a maturing but still sizable growth market, with sales expected to rise from $4.9tn in 2026 to $6.4tn in 2031 at a +6% CAGR. The note favors scaled platforms as share consolidates, with ancillary high-margin streams such as retail media, logistics, subscriptions, and seller services driving Commerce 3.0 margin expansion. For LatAm, GS expects faster growth than mature regions, with eComm +28% y/y in 2026 and +18% avg annual growth in 2026-28E, MELI reaching ~47% Brazil share in 2026E, and TikTok Shop still low-single-digit share after Mexico/Brazil launches.
important_observations: Scale remains the key investment filter: GS expects top platforms to keep consolidating share as mature eComm shifts from pure retail to broader consumer/merchant ecosystems.
LatAm and India are the highest-growth regions given low online penetration, while US/China still drive >50% of absolute global growth dollars.
MELI is positioned as the clear LatAm leader, with GS estimating ~47% Brazil share in 2026E despite Shopee at ~19% and TikTok Shop gradually building scale.
Retail media is highlighted as a high-margin rev stream, supporting the view that mature platforms can expand profitability even as core GMV growth normalizes.
Agentic commerce is early, with low adoption but high-intent use cases; GS sees both external LLMs and on-platform agents as eventual shopping surfaces.

US eComm expected +5% CAGR to ~$1.7tn in 2031; AMZN share forecast ~44% by 2028.
India eComm GMV estimated ~$100bn in CY26E; quick commerce share expected ~34% of India eComm by FY30E vs 15-20% today.

reports.headline: App Store MTD growth modestly reaccelerated and iPhone builds look better than feared, but iPad, PC/NB and IBM Consulting trackers weakened.

reports.title: AlphaWise Parcel Flight Tracker (August 2026)
reports.headline: Aug parcel flight data gave back July strength at FDX/UPS; MS sees likely pull-forward/payback rather than clear fresh demand deterioration.
reports.summary: MS AlphaWise August Parcel Flight Tracker showed sharp seq decel for FDX and UPS after July outperformance, with FDX domestic flights -7% seq and +2% y/y vs +7% y/y in Jul, and UPS -8% seq and -5% y/y. MS frames the reversal as more likely partial payback/pull-forward from July strength than a standalone demand deterioration, though it flags the need for 1-2 more months of data. AMZN normalized closer to seasonal trend at +5% seq and +4% y/y, while y/y growth continued to decel.
important_observations: FDX and UPS both gave back essentially all of July's seq beat, creating a sharp negative swing vs normal Aug seasonality.
MS does not yet read the Aug data as decisive evidence of fresh demand deterioration, but acknowledges possible incremental softening.
AMZN improved seq after two months of underperformance, suggesting parcel weakness was more acute at traditional parcels than AMZN in Aug.
Next 1-2 months of tracker data are key to separate July pull-forward/payback from broader demand softening.
new_data: FDX domestic flight count -7% seq in Aug vs +7% seq in Jul; +2% y/y vs +7% y/y in Jul; typical Aug seasonality +6% seq.
UPS domestic flight count -8% seq in Aug vs +8% seq in Jul; -5% y/y vs +1% y/y in Jul; typical Aug seasonality +5% seq.
AMZN domestic flight count +5% seq in Aug vs flat seq in Jul; +4% y/y vs +7% y/y in Jul; typical seasonality +6% seq.

reports.title: AI Wars: Google stable while ChatGPT had largest m/m back to school AI boost
reports.headline: BofA maintains Buy and $430 PO as Aug alt data show Google search usage stable despite ChatGPT's back-to-school AI bump.
reports.summary: BofA argues GOOGL search usage remains resilient as Aug web traffic, mobile DAUs, and search-share data show Google broadly stable while AI platforms keep growing from smaller bases. ChatGPT saw the largest m/m AI boost, likely helped by school starts, but Google web traffic was flat m/m and +3% y/y globally/US, with global mobile DAUs +12% y/y. Search share slipped m/m but was still up y/y, supporting the view that AI adoption is expanding the broader search market more than directly displacing Google NT. Investor focus is expected to shift to Sep/Oct ad checks as ChatGPT ads ramp, while OpenAI Astra, Meta Hatch, and Gemini 4 are upcoming sector catalysts.
important_observations: Google traffic and user growth were largely stable in Aug despite strong AI-platform growth, reinforcing the resilience side of the AI-search debate.
ChatGPT's m/m acceleration looks seasonal/back-to-school aided, but its scale is now large enough that ad monetization will draw more investor attention.
Google's search share softened m/m globally and in the US, especially desktop, but remained up y/y, limiting evidence of meaningful displacement so far.
AI adoption appears to be expanding search/query activity rather than simply shifting usage away from Google NT.
Sep/Oct ad-check calls are flagged as a bigger potential datapoint for ChatGPT ad monetization risk to the broader digital ad market.
new_data: Similarweb Aug global daily avg web visits: Google +3% y/y, flat m/m to 2.8bn; ChatGPT -5% y/y, +4% m/m to 181mn.
US web visits: Google +3% y/y, flat m/m to 534mn; ChatGPT +13% y/y, +4% m/m to 32mn, ~6% of Google.
Sensor Tower global mobile DAUs: Google +12% y/y, flat m/m to 2.3bn; ChatGPT +37% y/y, +5% m/m to 469mn; Gemini +284% y/y, +6% m/m to 126mn.
Aug net DAU adds: Google +3mn, ChatGPT +21mn, Gemini +7mn, Claude +0.4mn; Meta AI down, Grok flat.
Statcounter: Google global search share down 30bps m/m but +113bps y/y to 91.0%; US share down 60bps m/m but +29bps y/y to 86.0%.
Downloads: ChatGPT global app downloads +11% m/m to 76mn; Google +2% m/m to 10mn; ChatGPT/Google download ratio rose to 7.3x globally and 4.3x in US.

reports.title: Personal Assistant launch provides assist to stock; Maintain Buy
reports.headline: META’s Muse AI agent launch is framed as an important consumer AI proof point, with potential stock re-rating upside if traction and reliability follow.
reports.summary: BofA maintains Buy and $810 PO on META after the launch of Muse, a personal AI agent available across iOS, Android, web, and WhatsApp in the US with free and paid tiers. The note argues Muse is a major test of META’s ability to convert AI capex into consumer utility, with potential upside from referrals across META’s 3.5bn-user ecosystem, WhatsApp usage, subs, ads, or future AI capacity monetization. Key debates are whether users trust Muse with sensitive data/actions, whether the app can differentiate vs other AI assistants, and whether agentic commerce disrupts or helps internet marketplaces NT.
important_observations: Muse can autonomously execute multi-step tasks including email, travel booking, purchases, and project mgmt, with approval gates for sensitive actions.
Stock rose 6% intraday vs S&P 500 down 0.4% after the news, suggesting investors viewed the launch as an AI monetization proof point.
BofA sees Muse as one of META’s most significant consumer AI launches and a test of whether AI investment can produce differentiated user experiences.
Referral traffic from META’s 3.5bn users and WhatsApp distribution could help adoption if reliability and utility are strong.

Agentic AI launches are renewing concerns for eCommerce/travel marketplaces around direct traffic, share, and ad rev, though BofA expects larger incumbents to benefit NT from low-cost agent integrations.
new_data: META launched Muse in the US across iOS, Android, web, and WhatsApp.
Muse includes a free tier plus paid Power at $20/month and Maximum at $100/month.
Muse runs on a dedicated secure VM and offers permission controls, connected-app mgmt, and data-usage controls.
Early employee feedback cited strong functionality but also privacy and reliability issues.
Next catalysts cited are Meta Connect on Sep 23 and new LLM Watermelon expected in Oct.

reports.title: TSMC: August sales on track; 3Q likely to reach mid-high end of guidance amid tight leading-edge capacity
reports.headline: Aug sales keep 3Q26 on pace for mid/high end of guide; tight N3/N5, AI accel demand, and pricing support LT growth and margins.
reports.summary: JPM says TSMC Aug rev was NT$514.8bn, +53% y/y and +10% m/m, putting 3Q26 at ~67% of JPMe/cons and tracking to the mid/high end of US$44.6-45.8bn guide. The key update is worsening N3 tightness into 2027 despite ~40% capacity growth, driven by NVIDIA Rubin/Vera, agentic AI CPUs, and ASIC ramps. JPM expects mid/high-60s GM to hold despite N2 dilution, aided by leading-edge UTR, N3 GM improvement, and expected 2027 price hikes. Rating remains OW with NT$3,200 Jun-27 PT.
important_observations: Datacenter AI demand visibility now extends into 2029-30, supporting sustained growth view.
N3 supply/demand gap is expected to widen in 2027 despite major capacity adds, increasing likelihood of further capex upside.
NVIDIA could take 55-60% of total N3 wafer supply in 2027, up from <10% in 1H26, as Rubin/Vera ramps.
Mgmt/industry narrative implies TSMC retains front-end tech leadership; no meaningful Intel wins seen near term.
Advanced packaging competition may emerge, but CoWoS and SoIC remain key capacity bottlenecks and strategic focus areas.

reports.title: TSMC (2330.TW): Communacopia + Technology 2026 — Key Takeaways
reports.headline: Mgmt reinforced early-stage AI demand, Arizona execution, and confidence in 56%+ LT GM despite N2/overseas dilution.
reports.summary: GS highlights TSMC mgmt commentary from Communacopia + Technology 2026: AI remains an early multi-year megatrend, lower compute/token costs should drive more silicon consumption, Arizona Phase 1 is producing Taiwan-comparable yields and profits, and customers increasingly value geographic flexibility enough to support pricing. Mgmt remains comfortable with 56%+ LT GM despite 2-3ppt N2 ramp dilution and rising overseas fab dilution, supported by util, productivity, cost reduction, disciplined cap planning, and value-based pricing.
important_observations: AI exposure likely broader than disclosed because TSMC excludes CPUs/networking from its AI rev definition despite agentic AI potentially driving demand across those chips.
Arizona Phase 1 profitability and Taiwan-comparable yields reduce investor concern that TSMC’s manufacturing model cannot travel.
Mgmt expects ~30% of N2-and-beyond capacity outside Taiwan in five years, mainly Arizona, while most advanced nodes still ramp first in Taiwan.
N3 demand remains unusually persistent versus prior node cycles, with further capacity additions still unlikely to fully satisfy demand.
Cross-node capacity optimization, including N5 capacity supporting N3, is framed as an underappreciated manufacturing advantage.
Advanced packaging is treated mainly as a wafer-demand enabler rather than a standalone profit pool; CoWoS remains tight.
new_data: Arizona Phase 1 using N4 is operating with Taiwan-comparable yields, satisfactory quality/reliability, and positive profitability.
Equipment move-in for Arizona Phase 2 N3 expected soon; Phase 3 construction started; Phase 4 and first US advanced-packaging facility in preparation.
TSMC acquired additional Arizona land that could support another 5-6 fabs and the recently announced incremental US$100bn investment.
Current advanced-packaging capability supports ~5.5x reticle size, with roadmap to ~14x within several years.
N2 expected to dilute 2026 GM by ~2-3ppts; overseas expansion expected to dilute GM by 2-3ppts early in five-year period, widening to ~3ppts later.
management_insights: Mgmt says customer/customer-customer discussions and recent US CSP visits support confidence in AI infra readiness, including power and deployment plans.
Mgmt believes lower token costs from open-source models and compute efficiency will expand AI consumption rather than reduce silicon demand.
Mgmt says customers’ geographic-diversification asks have increased as Arizona execution has improved, and customers are increasingly willing to pay a premium.
Mgmt does not see a visible technical barrier to continued transistor scaling beyond N2 and A14 roadmap.
Mgmt wants one TSMC culture across Taiwan/US sites, with Arizona hires training 6-18 months in Taiwan.

reports.title: Meta Platforms Inc: The Models and Agents are Here; Upgrading to Overweight, $820 PT
reports.headline: JPM upgrades META to OW and lifts Dec-27 PT to $820 from $640, arguing frontier models, Muse agent traction, and Model API access create underappreciated AI upside despite major capex/FCF pressure.
reports.summary: JPM upgrades META to OW from Neutral and raises PT to $820, framing the company as early in monetizing frontier AI models beyond ads via Muse AI agent and Meta Model API. The note argues META’s distribution to ~4B users, privacy/security positioning, and faster model cadence improve its odds in consumer and enterprise AI, while core ads still have AI-driven upside. The main offset is sharply higher AI infra spend, with 2027-28 capex well above cons and negative FCF expected before new AI product monetization is modeled.
important_observations: JPM believes META’s model cadence has accelerated materially, with Muse Spark 1.3 now competitive with Claude/GPT models and Watermelon expected to expand product and monetization opportunities.
Muse AI agent showed strong early traction, reportedly reaching #3 in the US app store on day 2 and early usage running 10x training cohorts.
META’s ~4B-user distribution is viewed as a major advantage for consumer AI adoption, with potential monetization via take rates/commissions and subs over time.
Security/privacy are framed as a potential differentiator for agentic tasks involving passwords, credit cards, and personal info.
JPM expects AI compute needs to pressure FCF materially in 2027-28, but current model excludes new AI product monetization, leaving upside optionality if adoption converts to rev.

JPM anticipates negative FCF of $65B-$70B in each of 2027 and 2028.
management_insights: META has indicated it will maximize compute capacity in 2026 and 2027, with more flexibility in 2028+.
Mgmt’s 2025 goal in rebuilding MSL was to deliver frontier models within a year; JPM believes the team has essentially delivered.
Monetization is not the NT priority for Muse, but JPM sees LT opportunities in commissions/take rates and subs.
